Subject: Azerbaijan - introductions
Body:
Dear Hande 
It was great to speak with you yesterday and thanks for taking the time - you must be beyond busy in Baku!!
As promised, please find here our Health capacity statement, that explains the implementation support we provide to our partners across various health areas, all aligned with the objectives set out in GPW 14 (we even feature in para 18 ;)  
Our mandate is infrastructure, procurement and project management where we deliver around USD 3 billion per year in around 100 countries - over a third of which is focused in the health sector. As you rightly mentioned, UNOPS has provided limited support in Azerbaijan, primarily for TB drug procurement (we also host Stop TB and AT Scale that AZE govt contributes to). 
With this email, please also e-meet my UNOPS colleagues, Tim Lardner, the Regional Director for Europe and Central Asia, Freya von Groote Director of the Vienna multi-country office (Azerbaijan falls under her portfolio) and Sophie Djugeli, regional partnerships specialist.
Dear Tim
Please meet Hande Harmanci, the WHO Representative in Azerbaijan. During COP29, Hande will spend most of her time at the WHO Pavilion and I have flagged our Friday 9am "Energising healthcare" session to her which she said she will try to attend. Jorge met DG Tedros in Copenhagen last week at the European Regional Committee meeting, they discussed our collaboration specifically around solarisation of health facilities, working in fragile settings, health procurement and access to oxygen infrastructure. I understand Jorge is also meeting MOH AZE in Baku.
I hope you will be able to meet and discuss potential synergies!
All best wishesLouise

Dear Agnes and Sally,
I am reaching out to you to inform you that our local Jerusalem office has received the attached letter from our FCDO colleagues in Jerusalem. I understand that other UN agencies have received a similar letter. 
In the letter we are made aware of upcoming reporting requirements under UK legislation. Unfortunately these additional reporting requirements are beyond the terms and conditions that have been agreed in the already signed agreement. And as you are aware, UN entities are not strictly, legally bound by UK legislation. 
This being said, we are naturally always more than happy to provide as much information as possible upon requests from our trusted partners such as the FCDO. We therefore intend to continue to adhere to the current legal agreement and the clauses therein on eg. proactive management and reporting to protect UK aid from fraud and aid diversion, zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment, etc. 
I remain as always at your disposal for any follow-up inquiries. 
All the best,Asbjørn

Dear Jakob
Thank you for your response and valuable considerations on the way forward. 
We are consulting a wider group of our legal experts and will provide additional written elaborated explanations in Ukrainian on the 4 remaining disagreements in the draft legal agreement with CCD (as an agreement with the contractor has been reached). Based on that, Teressa and Svitlana will meet with the CCD again on Tuesday next week to make another attempt to reach an agreement. Following this meeting we will consult with you again on the way forward. 
We are very conscious of the fact that the CCD by the end of the day will be the formal recipient of the final reconstructed Arkas High School - and therefore has to be closely involved in the entire process, taking into account all of their input, technical advice, requests, etc. It is therefore crucial for the success of the reconstruction project that all parties (Denmark as the donor, UNOPS as the project manager, the contractor(s) and the CCD as the final recipient) are aligned. To ensure this we have for example incorporated legally binding requirements of monthly CCD inspections of the work. 
We are flagging the issues on contractual disagreements to you now, as the negotiations with the contractor and the CCD have been ongoing for a long time with more than 20 iterations at working level with the CCD alone. If Teressa and Svitlana are not able to reach a workable solution with the CCD next week at their level, I believe that we need to escalate the matter. Otherwise I fear that too much time will be lost without substantive progress. 
We may therefore need to call upon your help to escalate the matter with the local Ukrainian authorities to ensure that an amicable solution is reached with an agreement without potential conflicts of interests and a minimized risk assessment. 
As outlined in Teressa's document (attached here for ease of reference), the contractor was selected after a public tender process approved by CCD. The contractor has requested that all communication between the contractor and CCD happens via UNOPS as the project manager - which would ensure arms length and avoid potential conflicts of interests, etc. 
To specify the outstanding points, I have reiterated them below: CCD requests that UNOPS can only pay the contractor upon approval from CCDwould be a violation of UN financial rules and regulationsUNOPS would in practice lose control over the projectwould severely increase financial risk assessment

CCF requests the right to terminate the agreement with the contractor unilaterally with a notice period of 30 daysunacceptable to contractorcould create unfortunate conflicts of interests between contractor and CCDin violation with UN financial rules and regulations as UNOPS is the entity contracting UNOPS would in practice lose control over the project

CCD is to be the technical author and supervisorwhile CCD certainly should provide technical advice, requests, input, observations and must be consulted regularly (see agreement on monthly basis), the technical supervision of the reconstruction project has to be done by UNOPS as the project manager and as the responsible entity for ensuring the quality of the final product

Contractor has to eliminate defects after the first 12 months of finalising the projectthe defects notification period that can be accepted by UNOPS is 12 months which is standard for these types of infrastructure reconstruction projectsduring the first 12 months after finalising the reconstruction, flaws, etc. can be notified to UNOPS and we will make sure that it is dealt with within the 12 months period. For this reason we will only make the final payments to the contractor(s) after the 12 months defects notification period. We would be very happy to jump on a call at your convenience to elaborate on the matter. Otherwise I would suggest that we touch base during next week. 
We remain as always at your entire disposal for any comments, questions, requests or otherwise. 
All the best,Asbjørn

Dear Sune,
Many thanks for your detailed review and the readiness to proceed with the project from December onwards - subject to the completion of the proposal and the agreement of course.
On the proposal: We have so far not extended the scope of works. We still anticipate the major findings from the engineers to be reflected in the needs assessment report, which will follow the launch of the project and will form a basis for the exact scope. Based on the latest trip though, we tentatively estimate that the existing funds will not suffice to cover all anticipated works, hence we would be cautious to add new sites to the project at this stage.
On the specific emergency shelters, our engineers have concluded that:City Children Hospital No. 2 - the shelter repair works are at the final stage already, funding is provided by the city authorities and other donors.City Hospital No. 4 - the shelter repair works are in progress, works are finished in more than one-third of the premises.City Hospital No. 3 - anti radiation shelter needs structural construction works and water insulation works the cost of which is beyond the budget.In view of this, we would suggest to perhaps consider the inclusion of the anti-radiation shelter for the Hospital No.3 at a later stage as a further amendment to the project, if additional funds will be available, but refrain from the expansion of the scope for now, but let us know if this approach makes sense.
In the draft agreement, we have updated the text as per your comments, added the detailed budget  and the references to respective percentages. We also corrected some detected errors in the draft agreement and streamlined it to better reflect the distinction between the 2 projects. 
I hope these changes respond to your comments and make sense. 
Looking forward to your feedback.
With many thanks and kind regards,Elene

Subject: Re: Updates from the World Bank Group Annual Meetings
Body:
Dear Jorge, 
I hope you enjoyed your weekend. Now that the Annual Meetings are over, I am sharing an updated list of all our write-ups (plus audio podcast wrap-up) from the past week. 
Day 1: Key themesDay 2: Focus on energy and climateDay 3: Spotlight on IDA and WBG reformsDay 4: IFI/MDB cooperationDay 5: Podcast wrap-upGiven the significance of the initiative, I'm also sharing below some further information on Mission 300. WLO will be sure to follow up with relevant teams in HQ and the regions to raise awareness around Mission 300 and to support UNOPS' positioning.
Mission 300Alongside the African Development Bank, the WBG announced a new target at the 2024 Spring Meetings to connect 300 million people in Africa to electricity by 2030: now branded as Mission 300. The WBG has pledged $25bn in financing so far; AfDB $5bn. 
The Rockefeller Foundation, Sustainable Energy for All and the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet are also partners. These partners are leading a technical assistance facility to support governments.Energy Compacts are the primary vehicle to realise Mission 300. Fifteen pilot countries (including Nigeria, Senegal, DRC, and Côte d’Ivoire) are engaged in the Compact planning process, and will present their finalised plans to MDBs and donors in Tanzania in January 2025. At the summit, a second cohort of countries will be announced. (That the Compacts are country-level initiatives demonstrates the ongoing relevance of the country-driven model for the WBG). Compacts consist of five pillars. (Highlights indicate areas where UNOPS may add most value):Expand generation and invest in infrastructure at competitive costsLeverage benefits of increased regional integrationEmbrace distributed renewables (DRE) and clean cooking solutions to increase affordable last mile access.Incentivize private sector participation to unlock additional resources.Work towards financial viable utilities that provide reliable service.Affordability is a critical issue to ensure communities that are connected to energy can sustain their access. WB Regional Director for Infrastructure for Eastern and Southern Africa Wendy Hughes highlighted the role of competitive procurement tenders as one of the key ways to ensure competitive pricing. She also mentioned mini-grid/off-grid solutions, stating that these were normally driven by the private sector. 
Full write-upWLO would be happy to answer any further questions you may have about the Annual Meetings and next steps.
Best wishes,
Alistair

I hope you are well. Emilie asked me to send you the internal updates I have been preparing each day during this week's World Bank Group-International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings in Washington. 

We are pleased to see that procurement has been front and centre in several high-level panels, including one with President Banga. Procurement is clearly emerging as an important area as the WBG seeks to simplify its processes and ensure greater coherence of approaches across MDBs and other donors. This is part of the broader "Better Bank" agenda to increase the speed and efficiency of WBG operations. This week we are also tracking discussions around the new WBG Corporate Scorecard, the "Mission 300" effort to connect 300M Africans to electricity by 2030, and the IDA replenishment. The Scorecard is a particularly important development for UNOPS, given our organisation's efforts to focus on people-centred results measurement.

Subject: World Bank SFAs - no agreement yet reached - case-by-case approach will continue
Body:
Dear all: 
Thank you for your assistance over the past week in updating WLO on urgent SFA cases. 
No long-term agreement has yet been reached with the World Bank on the SFAs. We learned this afternoon (31 October) in a meeting with the Bank lawyers that the 31 October/1 November deadline will not be enforced. This is because the World Bank's leadership has not signed off internally on all the various provisions, nor have UN agencies seen the full text of the proposed framework agreement. To that end, we will continue on a case-by-case basis under the interim solution for urgent cases and work across LG, PLG and other relevant units to reach a final template. 
In the meantime, please continue to update the Google Sheet and to reach out to Christine and me with any urgent questions. 
We will keep you posted as discussions with the World Bank continue. 
Best wishes,
Alistair 
On Fri, Oct 25, 2024 at 4:36 PM Alistair Peter SOMERVILLE <alistairs@unops.org> wrote:
Dear all: 
I am writing to all country office focal points for WB-financed projects currently under consideration for the SFA "interim solution".
WLO has four brief requests of you going into next week to support our collective efforts to get these important projects over the line:
1. Update the expected signing date (column F)2. Update the notes in column L, especially any roadblocks you are facing in your interactions with the WB TTL/governments. You can also share these with myself and @Christine BOWERS over email, ideally with the name of the TTL so we can help move this along inside the WB.  3. Track down the WB Project ID in the project documents and add it to column D, if at all possible. This will significantly speed up the process to consolidate these requests and secure timely action from WB HQ. 4. Add myself and Christine to any Jira tickets for your urgent projects. 
More broadly, we do not expect to have a finalised new standard template by the end of October. Based on conversations with the World Bank, we are hopeful that for those projects already under discussion for the interim solution, we will be able to continue the case-by-case approach until a corporate solution is found. In any event, there is no expectation that government counterparts will need to have signed the agreements by the end of this month -- that can happen after 31 October in these cases. 
Thank you for your cooperation and we look forward to supporting you in the coming weeks. 
Have a lovely weekend!

Alistair

Subject: Suggested way forward for Danish Funded Secondment to UNSG's Climate Action Taskforce
Body:
Dear Marie-Louise and Lars,

First of all on behalf of UNOPS I wish to repeat my sincere apologies for the unsatisfactory process for the secondment of Ms. Lorentzen to the Climate Action Taskforce. I fully recognise your frustration for the situation that Ms. Lorentzen has been put in due to miscommunications between us, the Climate Action Taskforce and the Danish MFA. 

As discussed yesterday we now need to find the best option to remedy the situation as fast as possible and with the best possible conditions for Ms. Lorentzen. 

As the initially discussed secondment option means that Ms. Lorentzen would be liable for taxes, insurance and social security we propose two alternative options for the contract modalities:  
Fixed-Term Appointment: This option would take approximately 6 to 8 weeks, as it requires going through a competitive process, including a technical test. We will do our utmost to fast-forward the process as much as possible. This option provides more security in terms of taxes, insurance, and contract renewability.

Start with a Consultancy Contract (a fast tracked desk review): This option would cover an initial period of 6 to 9 months. The expected salary ranges from $8,500 to $9,400, depending on her years of experience. However, she would be responsible to pay for medical insurance and tax filings (which could be up to approx. 30%). Following this period, she could apply for the FTA position once it’s advertised.For the second approach, the Climate Action Taskforce would need to submit two substantially different Terms of Reference for the two positions. 

We await your decision on which option to proceed with - and remain at your entire disposal for any further clarifications.

Best regards,

Subject: Notes from ED meeting with Permanent Under-Secretary of State at the Danish Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Anders Tang Friborg
Body:
Dear colleagues,
On 21 October the ED met with the Permanent Under-Secretary of State at the Danish Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Anders Tang Friborg and Head of Foreign Affairs Department at the Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Henrik Winther. 
The ED initially informed about the situation in the Middle East, presenting the Gaza and UNVIM mechanisms as confidence building tools that could be useful to get the facts straight about the aid being delivered. 
Upon information from the ED, the Permanent Under-Secretary of State was positive towards the presented ideas on increased visibility about the tangible work done by the UN and the increased focus on implementation in connection with the CEB in Copenhagen in May 2025 - which would coincide with the Danish membership of the UN Security Council. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State would discuss the idea of a dialogue / fireside chat between the PM and the SG at the UN City in connection with the CEB. The Danish Government would try to utilise their membership of the Security Council to showcase what the UN could do - as the UN's reputation had diminished in recent years. It was therefore important to better show to the taxpayers what the UN could deliver. UNOPS was uniquely situated at this as the implementer of the UN system - headquartered in Denmark.  
It was agreed to resume the conversation once a full draft program for the CEB and the potential Helsingør Dialogue had been agreed upon between UNOPS and the Danish MFA. 
***
The situation in Gaza and YemenThe ED initially informed about the situation in Gaza and Yemen - explaining the Gaza Mechanism and the Yemen UNVIM as confidence building mechanisms that would enable better decision making based on factual data from the aid entering the conflict areas.  
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State afsked if it would be possible to scale the mechanisms for when the reconstruction efforts would start - which the ED confirmed although pointing to the fact that UNOPS could not guarantee the end use of the the products entering Gaza. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State mentioned that he had first encountered UNOPS during his time in Afghanistan. He had therefore followed UNOPS for a number of years. Initially it had been difficult to understand what UNOPS did, the business model, etc. But once he understood it, he had been impressed with UNOPS' ability to deliver tangible results on the ground - especially in difficult places such as Gaza and Afghanistan. 

S3iUpon a question from the Permanent Under-Secretary of State, the ED provided information about UNOPS' reform process since the S3i revelations. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State complemented UNOPS for the reform process - which could be a model for other UN agencies hit by crisis. 
UNOPS' mandateThe ED explained UNOPS non-programmatic mandate, focusing on the practical solutions and how the mandate was an enabler to work in special conflict areas such as Afghanistan, Sahel, etc. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State found this approach to be very much in line with Danish priorities and ways of working. 
CEB in Copenhagen and Helsingør DialogueThe ED committed to make the strong UN presence in Copenhagen more known to the broader public as the UN premises were funded by the Danish tax payers. A clear opportunity for this would be the upcoming CEB in Copenhagen in May 2025. The ED would try to maximise visibility which could for example be ensured by a dialogue or fireside chat between the Danish Prime Minister and the UN SG at the UN City back-to-back with the CEB. Such a dialogue could be open to the public/youth as well as the UN personnel based in Copenhagen - potentially also broadcasted publictly. 
The ED also presented the idea of a Helsingør Dialogue in connection with the CEB focusing on the implementation gap and the need to find practical solutions. Such a focus on the implementation would align well with the Danish pragmatic and solution focused approach. The ED mentioned that he had presented the idea to the Danish MFA State Secretary - offering to invite Denmark as the co-host. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State found the ideas of increased visibility interesting and the scope of focusing on the implementation gap to be fully in line with the Danish approach of making sure that big promises are translated into reality on the ground - finding pragmatic solutions. He committed to discuss the ideas with the PM and flagged that it could also be an opportunity for the PM to point towards the added value of the UN, some of the very tangible results and work done by the UN. This would be a topic for the Danish Membership of the UN Security Council - which would coincide with the CEB in Copenhagen. It might be worthwhile exploiting this. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State pointed out that although the Nordics had always been - and would remain - staunch supporters of the UN, it was clear that the reputation of the UN was diminishing. There was a clear need to showcase to the population what the UN could actually do. This was also a topic that the Danish Prime Minister had discussed with the UN Secretary General during UNGA a few weeks ago. 

The Permanent Under-Secretary of State would await for a draft program for the CEB coordinated between UNOPS and the MFA. Based on this, he would discuss with the Prime Minister. 
Finally the ED offered UNOPS' services and ability to provide objective data on eg. the situation in Gaza and Yemen to the Security Council during the Danish Membership. 

/Asbjørn

Kære Asbjørn



Som drøftet kommer her kort skitsering af forløbet omkring vores sekundering til EOSG/Climate Action Team (CAT).



Jeg sætter Lars og Tina på, der har haft kontakten til UNOPS og CAT, og som gerne giver mere baggrund.



Super nyttigt, hvis du har mulighed for at bistå. Vi har som sagt behov for, at den pågældende ansættes af FN, som det også normalt er tilfældet, herunder i lignende stilling tidligere.



Mange tak.



Bh Julia









I marts måned slog UM stillingen i EOSG/Climate Action Team (CAT) op som en FN-stilling, og FN oplyste i april direkte til Emma Siemens Lorenzen (på tidspunktet lokalansat på den danske FN-mission), at hun var udvalgt til stillingen. UM fik dog først oplysning herom i august til trods for, at vi op til flere gange, forsøgte at få en tilbagemelding fra FN.







FN havde derpå ifølge Emma Siemens Lorenzen løbende opfordret hende til at opsige sin stilling på missionen, så hun kunne starte hos CAT. Hun opsagde sin stilling med effekt fra 1.10. Ifølge Emma havde CAT stillet hende en kontrakt pr 1. oktober i udsigt. Samtidigt i september drøftede UM med FN formaliteterne, om hvordan Emma Siemens Lorenzen skulle ansættes. Stillingen har hele tiden været lagt op til en FN-ansættelse ligesom det var tilfældet ved en tidligere sekundering EOSG/CAT, men UNOPS ønskede formelt en dansk ansættelse. Relationen mellem UNOPS og CAT i sagen er ikke helt klar.







Dialogen om sekunderingsaftalen startede med Heba Najjar fra UNOPS (heban@unops.org<mailto:heban@unops.org>), hvorefter Marsha Cheddi (marsha.cheddi@un.org<mailto:marsha.cheddi@un.org>) fra CAT overtog dialogen pga spørgsmålet om, hvem der skulle ansætte. Den danske FN-mission ved DPR Erik Laursen gik i dialog med Cheddi om sagen, hvor det pr mail den 3. oktober (vedlagt) blev godkendt af CAT, at de ville ansætte Emma Siemens Lorenzen, således som ønsket fra dansk side.







Tirsdag den 8. oktober havde UM en samtale med Cheddi, der bekræftede, at CAT ville ansætte Emma under en multilateral sekundering, og i den forbindelse gav UM præcise oplysninger om Emmas anciennitet, civilstand og aktuelle bolig med henblik på, at de kunne beregne det præcise løntilbud til Emma. Det blev utvetydigt sagt, at Emma ville blive ansat af CAT på en kontrakt, der kan forlænges. Sideløbende med det meddelte UNOPS Emma, at hun ikke kunne ansættes af FN.







Torsdag vendte CAT tilbage efter samtalen tirsdag og nævnte, at stillingen skulle slås op igen kun for et år, og at Emma i stedet for kunne få en konsulentkontrakt indtil videre, da Emma nu ikke var ansat på missionen længere. Fra UM’s side gjorde man på ny opmærksom på, at det ikke var det, der var aftalt, og CAT undskyldte misforståelsen, men fastholdt at stillingen skal genopslås.







I fredags oplyste UM, at vi fastholdt, at CAT skulle ansætte Emma Siemens Lorenzen. Hertil har CAT oplyst, at de vil eskalere sagen, hvorved vi forstår, at de vil lade nogle højere i systemet afgøre det.







Vi forstår, at UNOPS kun kan modtage ’staff on loan’ som ’expert on mission’, og at det tilsyneladende er udfordringen med den konkrete konstruktion.

 the Annual Meetings approach, I wanted to highlight some of the key results from the project, particularly the timely delivery of key outputs to improve access to basic services and economic opportunities in a challenging FCV context: 





NCRP is reaching
 680,000 beneficiaries across 13 districts overall, including displaced people, host communities, and returnees.

35 local peacebuilding

5,000 people have

 workers (maternal and neonatal nurses, doctors, midwives) on prevention of gender-based violence (GBV) and sexual exploitation and abuse. The program includes support for case management and liaison with the justice system.


Training for teachers
 as health focal points within schools, with a focus on GBV, and mentorship for counselors and psychologists on GBV case management. 


In addition, 10,000
 youth have received technical skills training.

Subject: Notes from DED (D&P) meeting with Danish State Secretary for Development Aid, Ms. Lotte Machon
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On October 11 the DED (D&P) met with the State Secretary for Development Aid, Ms. Lotte Machon, at the Danish MFA. 
The State Secretary complemented the collaboration with UNOPS being very solution oriented, fast and agile - especially in Ukraine where UNOPS were implementing a significant part of the Danish aid. 
During the meeting it was agreed to gather 4-5 of the major Danish philanthropic foundations to discuss potential partnerships that could complement some of the Danish government's funded projects in Ukraine - following the format of the recent engagement with Novo Nordisk. 
The DED informed about the reform process and the upcoming dialogue about UNOPS' future vision and mission. The need to be better at measuring the impact of the work carried out by UNOPS was also discussed in relation to this.  
***
The DED initially informed the State Secretary about the discussions at UNOPS' GLN - where focus had been on the culture shift, partnerships and the future vision and mission for UNOPS. The State Secretary looked forward to an inclusive consultation process on the future vision and mission of UNOPS - and asked about the DED's first impression of UNOPS. 
The DED explained that the employees at UNOPS were extremely dedicated and very solution oriented. Unlike many other UN entities it was her impression that UNOPS employees were entirely focused on finding practical solutions to the problems at hand. There was however room for improvement in terms of measuring and communicating the quite significant impact of the work done by UNOPS throughout the world. The State Secretary agreed on the need to be better at measuring impact - but also pointed out that the most important part was the actual work on the ground. 
The State Secretary complemented the collaboration between Denmark and UNOPS - especially in Ukraine where she looked forward to the next 3 year programming period and hoped that UNOPS would continue to play a major role in the implementation of the Danish aid to Ukraine. The Danish Government was also very satisfied with UNOPS' rapid implementation of the Comprehensive Response Plan and looked forward to the independent review so that this chapter could be closed early 2025. 
The DED informed about the planning of the upcoming CEB in Copenhagen in 2025 and the ongoing reform process - pointing out that the digitalisation reform would take years as more investments had to be done over a number of years. 
The State Secretary emphasised the Danish Government's policy on more sustainable procurement practices - and desire to make the UN procurement more sustainable. The DED repeated the offer for a dedicated session with the PG on sustainable procurement - and how this could be improved further. The DED also asked the State Secretary to recall the sustainable procurement requirements when asking UNOPS to procure equipment on behalf of Denmark - not only focusing on time and speed. 
Upon a question from the State Secretary it was agreed that the DED and the State Secretary would soon gather 4-5 of the major Danish philanthropic foundations to suggest partnerships that would enhance the effects of some of the Dansh funded projects in especially Ukraine. The approach would build upon the recent experiences with Novo Nordisk, where the government funded the reconstruction of 6 hospitals and Novo Nordisk provided funding for the medical equipment, ambulances, machinery, etc. A similar approach could be done for the schools, where eg. Carlsberg  and LEGO might be interested in funding the school books, IT, furniture etc. NELO and the MFA Ukraine Division would provide a list with suggested projects by week 43 to initiate such a dialogue. 
Best,Asbjørn

Subject: Follow-up on meeting with UNOPS
Body:
Dear Ketil, 
It was an absolute pleasure meeting you and Emma on Friday 4 October. 
As mentioned by Dalila (cc) many of our operations are in some of the most challenging environments in Africa, including the Sahel and the Horn of Africa. UNOPS is the largest implementer of World Bank-financed projects in fragile, conflict, and violence-affected environments. This includes situations where the World Bank is unable or unwilling to fund governments directly due to political or financial constraints. In such cases, the World Bank channels funds through UNOPS to implement on behalf of donors, as seen in Afghanistan, Yemen, South Sudan, and Zimbabwe. We do similar setups for government donors. 
I am attaching a few factsheets for your information about our capacities and experience with projects on support to national governments and education that showcases our work supporting skills development and vocational training, UNOPS in the Sahel as well as one-pager about the two Danish funded projects in Somalia. 
As agreed, please find below a few short stories about some of the projects carried out by UNOPS in Africa. 
We look very much forward to continuing the dialogue. 

Best,Asbjørn 
Powering peace and sustainable development in West AfricaOn behalf of Sweden, UNOPS is bringing reliable and sustainable access to clean energy in rural areas of the Liptako-Gourma region of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.The project is providing access to clean and sustainable energy for over 300,000 people, and is implemented in collaboration with UNDP and the Liptako-Gourma Authority. UNOPS is responsible for the installation of 6 mini-grids – two in each country – and we are leading the development of local capacity that will ensure that the new systems can be effectively operated and maintained in the longer term. This is a three year pilot project. 
Zimbabwe Idai recovery projectThe Zimbabwe Idai recovery was a four-year project, where UNOPS managed a $72 million World Bank fund and worked together with UNICEF, FAO, WHO, WFP, IOM, UNFPA and UNESCO. The project aimed to build the foundations for regional recovery after Cyclone Idai hit Zimbabwe. 
Around 50,000 households were destroyed and more than 60,000 people were displaced. Nine districts faced up to $622 million in damages. The approach of this project was to help the community not just to recover what was lost - but be able to mitigate future shocks. 
The results of the projects include: rehabilitation of health facilities, water systems and sanitation facilities, schools, irrigation schemes, micro-watersheds and roads that connected people to services – all infrastructure that's vital to the more than 346,000 people in the impacted communities.integrated health services and gender-based violence response for more than 672,000 people, including more than 3,600 internally displaced people.local jobs, thus helping build community capacity and resilience by providing infrastructure development skills. Labor-intensive, community-focused infrastructure projects created job opportunities for more than 5,200 community members, nearly half of them women.training for local authorities on the operation and maintenance of the infrastructure that was built, ensuring it remains in good working order for communities.partners involved worked closely with Zimbabwe’s national and local government, to build stronger disaster risk governance and preparedness. This involved developing early warning and risk information systems to inform disaster risk preparedness and contingency planning.to ensure that the project laid the foundation for resilience to future shock and stresses, it involved a comprehensive climate hazard and risk assessment. It made sure to engage the local community’s views via a participatory design process. This approach informed the climate resilient and inclusive design and construction of community schools, roads, health facilities, irrigations and markets.
Reconstruction of social services in YemenFunded by the World Bank, this project restored access to critical services and strengthened resilience to shocks in selected urban cities in Yemen. The project follows an area-based approach for investment in tertiary municipal services, solid waste management, water, sanitation, roads, and electricity. The project targeted approximately 3 million beneficiaries.  UNOPS has designed and rehabilitated critical urban infrastructure damaged by the ongoing conflict, incorporating resilience against identified risks. This includes water, sanitation and solid waste systems, roads and electricity supply. UNOPS has rehabilitated more than 230 kilometers of roads in 8 cities and restored access to critical services for more than 3 million people. A key component of the project aims to boost the local economy and strengthen capacity by partnering with local Yemeni.
The results of the projects include: rehabilitation of over 450 km of urban roads.the enhanced road infrastructure improves road safety, while efficient water drainage systems and newly built retaining walls are designed to protect the road from structural damage and to mitigate the effects of climate change.the upgraded road plays a crucial role in connecting Amran city to Sadah and Hajjah, serving a population of over 200,000 people.to help improve sanitation and avoid health hazards for more than half a million people, UNOPS constructed more than 6 km of new sewage line in Yemen’s historic city of Sana’a
4. Support to Tunisia’s border control and management of migration flowsFunded by the Italian government, this project aims at supporting Tunisian authorities in the continued and improved control of maritime borders by enhancing operational capacities of the fast patrol fleet of the maritime National Guard.
With €15 million funding from the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, UNOPS is implementing this project to provide maintenance services for 6 of the Tunisian Maritime National Guard’s fast patrol boats, as well as the procurement of various equipment for the Tunisian Authorities.
UNOPS has continuously provided maintenance of 6 patrol boats over a period of two years. This includes: Ordinary maintenance (predictive)Extraordinary maintenance (corrective)Spare parts for six vesselsThe Tunisian authorities’ needs for equipment and supplies were fulfilled; UNOPS has procured and supplied equipment needed by the Tunisian Authorities to a maximum value of €31 million. I hope that some of these project examples give a good indication of some of the tangible value add of the projects we implement in Africa.

Subject: Re: Updated proposal for the full restoration of the Arkas High School
Body:
Dear Anne and colleagues, 
With regards to our conversation on when the children would be able to return physically to the Arkas High School, our estimate for a best-case-.scenario is September 2026 - whilst the worst-case scenario is December 2026. Due to the ongoing construction work it would not be responsible with a phased return for the children, as it would be a proper construction area with risks of accidents. 
With regards to our conversation on what would be the potential delays if the agreement on the full restoration of the Arkas High School is not signed before January 2025, we estimate that there would be no substantive delays in the reconstruction work. However, if the agreement will only be signed by mid/end February, it would lead to delays in the construction works. We would therefore suggest to finalise the conversation on proposal, agreement amendment, budget etc. before the end of 2024 - so that we are able to sign it as soon as possible in January 2025. 
Elaborating about the timelineThe long-term stabilization is estimated to last 10 months. We should have started, but we are struggling with the local authorities to get the permits, which are more challenging than expected. Teresa and colleagues in Kyiv will reach out to the Danish embassy to get assistance if today's meeting is not productive. 
We can begin the restoration work approximately 6 months after starting the stabilization (during the last 4 months of the stabilization). The full restoration, which includes finishing the bomb shelters, is estimated to take 21 months. We will try to reduce it to 18 months, but we cannot promise this for now. Naturally we will continue to keep you in the loop throughout the process. 
We look very much forward to hearing back from you - and remain at your entire disposal for follow-up inquiries, comments, etc. 
Best regards,Asbjørn

Body:
Dear Kateryna,
I hope this email finds you safe and well.
I am writing to inquire about any recent developments regarding the HOME programme since our last meeting.
I also wanted to update you on our partnership with AT Scale. This Global Partnership for Assistive Technologies aims to catalyze action, amplify existing work, and coordinate global stakeholders to increase the availability of and access to assistive technology. AT Scale has extensive experience in the field of Assistive Technologies and has received requests from the Ministry of Health to provide targeted assistance in enhancing equitable access to high-quality prosthetic and orthotic (P&O) services in Eastern Ukraine.
To this end, we have developed a joint Concept Note, which is enclosed with this email. Subject: Follow up on the meeting regarding the potential cooperation

Corporate Use






Dear Elene
 
Thank you very much for your time, fruitful discussion we had and the information you provided.
 
As we discussed, the EIB is currently considering number of options to ensure the provision of TA at the municipal level for the implementation of upcoming Programme on financing
 social and affordable housing in Ukraine. As agreed, we will continue further consultations with you to better understand the possibility for our potential engagement.  Please, see below the synopsis of TA tasks expected to be delivered at the municipal level:
 






TA teams to provide advisory support and monitoring at the municipal level
to establish transparent and participatory mechanism of project implementation at all phases of project cycle, including:


capacity development and day-to-day support to Project Implementation Unit in municipalities,
support to the technical documentation development, including preparation/monitoring of project design documentation, verification, authors supervision.

technical design checking, with the specific attention to the “Build Back Better” and comprehensive EE solutions in the design and implementation,
procurement related capacity development (incl. procurement plan and tender documentation),

support in identifying implementation issues (social, environmental, corruption, sanctions, etc.)
support in organising regular technical working groups and track progress with identification of any bottlenecks in implementation with proactively proposing solutions of acceleration
 implementation and disbursement,
support in oversight and monitoring of the quality of construction works, including:



collecting and providing an information to EIB, Ministry, Promoter and Final Beneficiaries detailed technical and financial information on individual housing projects (new construction),
 including maturity, timeline, project cost and sources of financing, technical parameters, land availability, environmental issues, social issues, tenders
physical control of implementation and progress in line with the initial plan/design, identification of social, environmental and procurement issues, including corruption.



social management and stakeholder’s engagement,
institutional development of municipally owned housing company

 

As we briefly discussed, we will suggest the additional meetings to explore the details of the expected TA services, in particular anti-corruption and sanctions checks, as well as other
 technical details, if it is fine with you.

 

Kind regards

 

Oksana.

Dear Oksana,
 
Thank you for the excellent meeting today. We truly appreciate the trust you place in UNOPS and are eager to partner with you in addressing the significant housing needs in Ukraine.
 
As promised, please find attached brief flyers outlining UNOPS' portfolio and ongoing projects in Ukraine. Not referred to here is the recently added World Bank-funded Health Enhancement
 And Lifesaving (HEAL) project, which is operational as of last week.  For context on our regional experience in social housing, you can review the EU-funded Social Housing and Active Inclusion (EU-SHAI) project implemented by UNOPS in Serbia here:
https://social-housing.euzatebe.rs/en/
 
I can indeed confirm that we have a robust legal framework in place to proceed with our partnership. The Master Agreement (attached, along with the Letter of Understanding) allows

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you require any further information.
We look very much forward to working closely with you in the coming weeks and months.


 


Kind regards,

Subject: Réunion agences Colead ENERGIE
Body:
Chers collègues Colead énergie,
Je suis Mahmoud Ghouil, le consultant-conseiller en planification stratégique pour appuyer le développement des programmes phares au Mali.
Je suis très heureux d'avoir fait votre connaissance lors des dernières réunions UNCT et des colead.
Je viens de lire avec beaucoup d'attention la note conceptuelle que vous avez préparée et je vous en remercie. Vous trouverez ci-après quelques commentaires pour discussion/ clarification. Ø Pour assurer une meilleur appropriation nationale:Impliquer davantage le gouvernement dans toutes les étapes du processus.Institutionnalisation  d’un mécanisme de gouvernance du programme ( Comité technique) coprésidé PNUD-UNOPS/ Ministère chargé de l'énergie avec des TDR précisant le rôle de chaque partie, AFP impliqués, BF potentiels avec la participation du groupe mobilisation des ressources.Ø A clarifier l'alignement des résultats avec le cadre de coopération et les cibles ODD A rappeler l’alignement avec le CF 2020-2024 et notamment l’axe 2 du cadre de Coopération et les cibles ODD priorisées dans ce domaine.Manque d'alignement entre résultats attendus du programme avec les priorités nationales selon les cadres de planification stratégiques et les cibles ODD priorisées  Agenda 2063 et points d’entrée programmatiques pour UN. Ø Revision des theories des changement à la lumière de la formation qui aura lieu le 7 novembre 2024 avec le bureau Régional Afrique A clarifier la relation entre les  objectifs/résultats et les composantesIl faudrait montrer la relation de cause à effet dans la chaîne des résultats en ajoutant des hypothèses pour la réalisation des changements souhaités.Utiliser une approche systémique en montrant l’interconnexion possible entre le domaine de l’alimentation, l’éducation et l’utilisation des énergies renouvelables avec des schéma si possible.Quelle est la complémentarité et synergies du programme par rapport à d’autres interventions des Nations Unies dans le même domaine ? Quelle est la synergie avec d’autres initiatives par les PTFs, IFIs, etc..dans le domaine cible ?Ø Le volet mobilisation des ressources se limite à estimer un coût global sans  précision de la nature de ces fonds ; FP ou à mobiliser auprès des BF Le montant alloué est relativement faible par rapport aux autres programmes phares.
Ø Absence de la dimension transfrontalière/ régionale du programme par rapport au pays du Sahel Central ?
L'objectif est d'avoir une  NC précise/concise 7 pages max qui sera discutée et validée avec le gouvernement et utilisée lors de l’atelier de planification.
Je voudrais également prendre contact avec vous au cours de cette semaine pour discuter notamment les points: 
Discussion sur les notes conceptuellesMécanisme de gouvernance (TDR comité technique ENERGIE) & préparation TDRDivers
Merci de bien vouloir m'indiquer par retour d'email le créneau qui vous convient pour la réunion.

Cordialement,
Mahmoud

Chers collègues
 
A la suite de l’atelier de planification stratégique pour l’élaboration des programmes phares organisé du 3 au 5 décembre à Bamako, je tiens à vous réitérer mes remerciements pour votre engagement
 à œuvrer pour le succès de cette initiative commune du Gouvernement du Mali et du Système des Nations Unies. Sous votre leadership, l’atelier a permis, entre autres objectifs, de valider les notes conceptuelles, les théories de changement, élaborer le cadre
 logique de résultats, proposer des mécanismes de gouvernance et établir un chronogramme pour les prochaines étapes qui seront essentiellement la finalisation des cadres logiques et la rédaction des documents de programmes.  Pour votre information je joins
 à ce courriel copies des lettres de remerciement que j’ai transmises aux différents Ministères.  
 
En me félicitant pour les efforts fournis par vous et les groupes de travail pour ces résultats tangibles obtenus, j’espère que les travaux de suivi avancent comme prévu et je voudrais également vous
 rappeler que DCO attend de nous des livrables pour chaque programme phare, dont un narratif de 2-3 pages maximum par programme avec un visuel (infographie table b déjà communiquée par le consultant pour mise à jour et validation).
 
Pour mener à bien ce travail, je vous vous invite à transmettre au RCO les documents clés suivants :
 
- une version validée de l'infographie table b d'ici la fin de journée comme convenu.
- le cadre logique des résultats qui tient compte des différents commentaires du Consultant,
- un narratif de 2 pages qui résume la note conceptuelle et qui reflète les résultats stratégiques du programme avec le plan ci-après :  (1) les défis (justificatifs avec chiffres
 clés sur la situation actuelle) ; (2) les résultats stratégiques en réponse aux défis annoncés en décrivant brièvement la théorie de changement (en tenant compte des hypothèses sur les domaines non couverts par le programme) et en précisant les changements
 sur la population cible et le système ; (3) Impacts attendus 
 
Si vous avez des questions plus détaillées ou toute autre clarification prière en parler avec Isidore et Mahmoud.
 
Bien à vous.
 
Khassim Diagne

Dear Neil,I hope you are doing well, Thank you for confirming DOWASCO’s acceptance of manual transmission Toyota Hilux pickups.We are coordinating closely with Toyota Global Supply (TGS), and before they can proceed with export approval to Dominica, Toyota Japan has requested specific information to complete the process. This is a necessary step prior to confirming the order. We kindly request your support with the following points:1. Warranty and Service Support

We confirm that Toyota does not have any official warranty coverage or service support in Dominica. Therefore, all warranty-related and maintenance costs will be fully borne by DOWASCO.

Our understanding is that similar arrangements have previously been managed by government entities in Dominica, given prior acquisitions of Toyota vehicles without local representation.2. Additional Information Required by Toyota Japan

To obtain export clearance, Toyota Japan has asked for:

Planned use: A short note describing how the vehicles will be used operationally.


Financing clarification: Toyota cannot proceed with a generic reference to “Caribbean Development Bank.” They require:


A short written explanation or official document describing the financing source; and


A written confirmation from DOWASCO that outlines the nature of the funds and their intended use.



I am also taking this opportunity to remind you about UNOPS Due Diligence Process, and the questionnaire that was submitted to DOWASCO for completion and return to UNOPS. Please keep in mind that without this process, we will not be able to move ahead.  Please let us know if any clarification is needed. We remain at your disposal and appreciate your continued collaboration.










Warm regards,

Antoine

나이지리아 근무하며 건축업무 유놉스와 협의를 진행해왔는데,결과적으로는 타 기관이 좀 더 저희 조건에 맞는 상황인 것으로 내부적으로는 정리 중입니다. 가장 큰 관건은 아무래도 유놉스 오버헤드 경비가 크다는 점이었어요.저희가 예산이 충분치 못하다보니 조건을 맞추는데 어려움이 있었습니다. 개인적으로는 협의과정에서 유놉스에 대해 아는 계기가 되었네요.
스리랑카에서 좋은일 많이 하시고, 성과도 많이 거두시기 바라고,언제든 또 좋은 기회에 인사드리겠습니다.
감사합니다.

손성일 선생님, 
안녕하세요. 기억하실지 모르겠는데, 이전에 한양대 석사 아마도 선생님보다는 다음 기수로 들어와서 수업때 여러번 뵀었던 김유경이에요. 이전에는 기아대책 다녔었고 선생님께 코이카 민협 사업 자료 공유해주셔서 도움 받았던 기억이 있어요. 잘 지내셨지요? 코이카 여러 분들 통해서 종종 선생님 소식 듣고 안부도 묻기도 했었는데, 직접 연락드리는 건 처음인 것 같아요. 
선생님 현재 나이지리아 사무소 계신것 맞으시죠? 저는 지금 유놉스 남아시아 사무소에서 근무하고 있고, 가끔 다른 지역에서 코이카와 협력할 때 지원 요청이 올 때가 있는데 1개월 전쯤 나이지리아 사무소에서 연락이 왔고, 확인해보니까 선생님께서 계시는 곳이더라고요. 너무 반갑기도 하고 유놉스 나이지리아 팀에서 요청도 있어서 이렇게 따로 메일 드리게 되었어요. :)  최근 코이카와의 협력 마지막 단계에서 중단된 상황이 있었다고 하더라고요. 그래서 유놉스 측에서 준비한 주요 자료들 저도 훑어보면서 제가 보기에도 몇 가지 아쉬운 부분들이 있긴 했었는데, 혹시 조금 더 배경을 알려주실 수 있을까 상황에 대해 조금 더 이해하고자 조심스레 문의드립니다. 유놉스 팀에서 간과한 부분이 있거나 개선해야할 점들 파악하는 것도 저희 팀에게 큰 도움이 될 것 같아서요. 
혹시 시간을 내어 말씀 나눌 수 있는 기회가 된다면, 편하신 시간에 맞추어 조율하겠습니다. 
이렇게 다시 연락드리게 돼서 너무 반가웠습니다. :)
